headline: Oklahoma basketball lives in high school gyms, and it was there before the Thunder
summary: Oklahoma basketball predates the Thunder. Black hoops pride runs through Tulsa's Booker T. Washington and OKC's Douglass. Native nations run their own gym-and-tournament circuits, and college loyalty splits four ways. The Thunder arrived in 2008 with no pro team ahead of them, so the whole state claims them. Meet that state in its gyms and high school stands, not only at Paycom Center.

insights.title: Fans drive in from Tulsa, Lawton and Norman
insights.detail: Apart from the Hornets' temporary 2005-07 stay after Katrina, the Thunder (2008) are the only major pro team Oklahoma has had, and in 2025 they gave the state a champion. Fans from Tulsa, Lawton, Norman and small-town gyms drive in for games. Rural and tribal communities claim the team as much as metro OKC does.
insights.implication: Plan events statewide, with Tulsa and Norman as real second and third hubs, not just Bricktown and Paycom Center.

insights.title: College loyalties run deeper than team colors
insights.detail: Sooners (now in the SEC), Cowboys, Tulsa and Oral Roberts each have loyal followings, and Thunder players with local college ties get claimed twice. Families often split blue-and-orange between Thunder and OSU.
insights.implication: Avoid orange-heavy and crimson-heavy product that reads as a college allegiance by accident. Anchor Thunder product in Thunder blue, sunset orange and yellow.

insights.title: High school hoops is community glue
insights.detail: Programs like Booker T. Washington in Tulsa, Douglass and Millwood in OKC, Edmond Santa Fe and Heritage Hall carry neighborhood pride. In March, the state tournaments fill arenas with whole towns.
insights.implication: School-spirit team sets and warm-ups for Oklahoma high school programs could quietly build credibility.

insights.title: Native basketball is a living tradition
insights.detail: Oklahoma is home to 39 tribal nations. School and community gyms in Native communities run their own tournaments and rivalries. Native players and families form a large and loyal Thunder base.
insights.implication: On any collaboration, work with Native designers and community organizations, credited and paid. Never lift ceremonial or sacred imagery.

insights.title: Development culture, not star-chasing
insights.detail: Under Sam Presti, the Thunder's identity is patient player development, with the OKC Blue as the G League feeder. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the back-to-back MVP, is its face. Fans take pride in drafted and developed players like Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and now Aday Mara.
insights.implication: Tell worker-bee, earned-not-given stories in campaigns. This market is allergic to flash that isn't backed by work.

insights.title: Gilgeous-Alexander bridges Hamilton and OKC
insights.detail: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is a Hamilton, Ontario native and back-to-back MVP. OKC embraces him as its own, as it did Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook in earlier eras. His sneaker and style choices lead local trends.
insights.implication: Signature and team-adjacent product tied to Gilgeous-Alexander is the strongest single hook in the market.

places.name: Paycom Center
places.why: Home of the Thunder and the OKC Blue, and the center of the state's basketball identity.

places.name: Lloyd Noble Center
places.why: Long-time home of Sooners basketball and the heart of the OU hoops fanbase.

places.name: Gallagher-Iba Arena
places.why: Oklahoma State's loud, old-school home, known as much for wrestling as for Cowboys basketball.

places.name: Mabee Center
places.why: Home of Oral Roberts basketball and the site of past Cinderella-run celebrations.

places.name: Douglass High School
places.why: Historic Black high school with deep community ties in Northeast OKC.

places.name: Booker T. Washington High School
places.why: Tulsa's storied Black high school program, home to the Wayman Tisdale legacy.

places.name: Deep Deuce
places.why: Historic Black jazz and cultural district, and a natural link between Thunder culture and OKC heritage.

places.name: Oklahoma State Fair Arena (Jim Norick Arena)
places.why: Long-time host of high school tournament action.

people.name: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander
people.why: The face of the franchise and the state's current basketball hero.

people.name: Chet Holmgren
people.why: Drafted and developed in OKC, the clearest example of the Thunder development story.

people.name: Jalen Williams
people.why: Homegrown through the draft and a major piece of the title core.

people.name: Wayman Tisdale
people.role: Tulsa-born OU star, NBA player and musician
people.why: A beloved Oklahoma basketball figure whose legacy is claimed statewide.

people.name: Blake Griffin
people.role: Former NBA All-Star, Oklahoma Christian HS and OU alum
people.why: Oklahoma-raised star claimed as a local great.

people.name: Trae Young
people.role: NBA All-Star, Norman North HS and OU alum
people.why: Another Oklahoma-built star that locals claim.

people.name: Kevin Durant
people.why: His OKC years shaped the franchise's early identity. Sentiment toward him is complicated.

people.name: Russell Westbrook
people.why: Remembered as a defining OKC icon whose fashion reshaped how locals and NBA players dress.

productHooks: Oklahoma gym-pride capsule: varsity-style warm-ups and tees in Thunder blue with red-dirt accents.
Gilgeous-Alexander team-adjacent drops, timed to opening night and the Cup run.
Statewide team-set program for high schools and community gyms, with Oklahoma schools and Native community designers as partners.
Prairie-sky gradient shooting shirt for summer league and pro-am season.
watchouts: Never use sacred or ceremonial Native imagery. Engage Native designers and organizations directly, and credit and pay them.
College marks (Sooners, Cowboys, Golden Hurricane, ORU) need licensing and can alienate the other half of a split-loyalty fanbase.
Sentiment on Kevin Durant and Russell Westbrook is complicated. Skip nostalgia product that reopens old wounds.
Don't treat Oklahoma as one place. Tulsa, OKC, Norman and rural communities each have their own identity.
